name: kittykeys
subtitle: An open-source keyboard for English and Hinglish

apps.name: kittykeys
apps.subtitle: An open-source keyboard for English and Hinglish
apps.localizedDescription: An open-source iPhone keyboard for English and Hinglish: a number row, symbols on long-press with hints on the keys, space-bar cursor control, an emoji panel with search, and no autocorrect, so Hinglish words stay as typed. Nothing you type leaves your phone.

versions.localizedDescription:
- Themes, like SwiftKey's: Settings › Theme has ten ready-made ones, including Neon (black, with neon green on shift, ⌫, 123, 😊 and return), Midnight, Amber, Synthwave, Terminal, Paper and Rose. Automatic, today's look, stays the default
- Make your own: tap New theme, or touch and hold a theme and choose Customise. Pick the background, the key style (filled, outlined or no borders), key colours and shadow, label colours, an accent (optionally on the return key), and the font and its weight, with a working keyboard at the top to try it
- Settings › In dark mode picks a separate theme for dark mode. iOS colours the strip with 🌐 and the microphone light or dark to match your phone, so a dark theme suits dark mode

- Try it has "Things to try": moving the cursor with the space bar, holding a key for its symbol, sliding left from ⌫ to delete a word, a text replacement, and emoji search. Each ticks itself the moment you do it with kittykeys
- Setup offers "Next: try it out" once both of its steps are done

- Web addresses: no separate .com key by default, so the space bar is full width; hold . for .com, .in, .co.in, .org or .net (also in email fields). Settings › Show a .com key brings the key back
- Currency: d and the 123 page offer your currency first, from your region or picked in Settings › Currency
- Setup shows a green tick for each step once it's done
- Try it can switch the field between text, email, web and number, to see how the keys change
- The typing test is gone

The first public release. catkeys is now kittykeys; updating keeps your settings and Recent emoji.

- Emoji panel: Recent, categories, skin tones on hold, and search
- Your Text Replacement shortcuts from iOS Settings expand after a space, return or punctuation; ⌫ right after puts the shortcut back
- In a one-time code field, kittykeys switches to the next keyboard so Apple's keyboard can offer the code from Messages; 🌐 brings kittykeys back (Settings › Switch to Apple's keyboard for codes)
- Settings shows the version, and Setup has an Open Settings button
- A typing test in the app, to compare keyboards
